title: Opus 5.5 One-shot - Roguelike Pixel Art Chess Game
author: Tasty-Ad-3753
selftext:
Prompt -> "Please make me a beautiful pixel art roguelike chess game - aim for 2h playtime but endless replayability, make me proud, make it fun, get creative, and really go all in on the pixel art graphics and motion design. Use [https://rpg-mote-studio.vercel.app/](https://rpg-mote-studio.vercel.app/) for the pixel art"

Opus 5.5 seems genuinely insane at making games with little-to-no supervision. I made two tweaks afterwards:

\- "Make it spawn a little less obstacles on the board - like 40% less. Also there's a bug with the pause menu I think maybe? Please check"

\- "Please reduce the difficulty by about 20%"

This is literally all the direction I gave to the model. Crazy! Everything else was one-shotted. If I was better at chess then I could have removed the second tweak haha.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body: It's never one shot. One shot is only possible if the ai knows what to do and that means copying something, in your case another game. Sorry to say but the is exactly what ai shouldn't be used for.

replies.author: TheFlynnCode
replies.body: That's not true w.r.t. what one shot means.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
One shot means giving a single prompt as input. And letting the ai do it's thing. 
Am I wrong?

replies.author: TheFlynnCode
replies.body:
You're right that that's what it originally meant. I think the term originated with older image classifiers as a technique for telling whether two images are of the same person/object, even if the person/object had never been seen by the model before.

  
Even in this case, the model is not copying something. It is using similarity measures on some latent representation that it has learned.

  
But more to the point with LLMs, but especially claude and gpt: these usually spin off several dozen / several hundred processes to answer a single question. So I wouldn't even necessarily call a one-shot prompt to create a video game "true one shot", whatever that means, but ignoring that, even if it was true one shot, it also would not be working off a memorization and doing copy/paste.

replies.body: True. But calling one shot = game dev is wrong in my eyes. It's a Prototyp top Start and nothing more

comments.author: Exciting_Lie_8370
comments.body:
First it is a cool project.
I still don't think it is easy to make a profitable game, but...
I don't wanna do a game jam anymore after  seeing this.
By the standard of a game jam, this is a pretty solid game, the kind would get a good score if the theme is correct.
And you didn't even provide a clear idea for it, just a very vague direction. 
Just thinking i might have to compete with such projects on a game jam feels...frustrating.

replies.author: Tasty-Ad-3753
replies.body:
For real! Not to sound too pessimistic myself but I'm 10000% certain that we will see automated content farms churning out games. Like as much as this tech will help humans to develop games and their passion projects, this game made me realise that the AI models can also be creative on their own and do things end to end.

Maybe not with opus 5.5 but I'm sure with Opus 6, people will start setting up automations where every day they produce multiple indie game style outputs and put them live, automate some kind of social media post, and hope one of them goes viral.

replies.author: Exciting_Lie_8370
replies.body:
What impressed me the most is how efficient it is on using tokens and how well it can do simple indie feeling art assets now.

Gameplay-wise and development-wise I think AI has been this good for a long time.

This is a good game only by the standard of a game jam or a demo, so it finished what a talented developer can do in a few days without feeling like an AI slop, which is impressive.

But games that actually can get popular, personally speaking, is still a long way ahead of this, which is what the developers can still do.

And now i think of it...most developers have boring ideas actually, so don't wanna blame AI too much on that. The market was filled with rip-off rogue-likes way before AI is good. More such games are likely to flood the market and consume each other.

For really talented folks can come up with creative and funny ideas, things might not change a lot.
